actions.action: Expire and remove records after at most five minutes.
actions.mechanism: Enforce a fixed deadline rather than extending freshness on access.
actions.implementation: Set expires_at using a monotonic clock when a successful source response is accepted, capped at 300 seconds. Check the deadline before serving; delete expired entries immediately. Schedule deadline-based deletion even without reads. Never renew the deadline on hits or failed fetches.
actions.check: With a fake clock, verify a record is unavailable at its deadline, repeated hits do not extend it, and an outage does not preserve expired entries.
actions.risk: Process pauses can delay physical cleanup; read-time checks must still prevent expired responses.

actions.action: Enforce the 100-record memory limit during fetches as well as caching.
actions.mechanism: Reserve bounded record slots before admitting source responses.
actions.implementation: Use a shared pool of 100 slots covering cached records and in-flight record buffers. Under an atomic admission operation, remove expired entries first, then evict the least-recently-used unreserved entry if needed. Reject admission when all slots are reserved. Release reservations on every failure path.
actions.check: Run concurrent misses, cancellations, and timeouts; assert occupied plus reserved slots never exceed 100 and all failed requests release reservations.
actions.risk: Counting only cache entries would miss temporary decoding copies; the implementation must account for these too.

actions.action: Return an explicit unavailable response when the source times out.
actions.mechanism: Bound waiting and separate source failure from record absence.
actions.implementation: Set a configurable source timeout within the request deadline. Serve an existing unexpired record without contacting the source. On a miss or expired entry, attempt the fetch; on timeout return HTTP 503 with a stable source_timeout code. Remove expired entries, retain unrelated unexpired entries, and never cache the failure as a record.
actions.check: Simulate a hanging source: misses return 503 within the configured deadline, valid hits still work, and expired records are neither returned nor retained.
actions.risk: A timeout that is too short can reject source requests that would otherwise succeed.

actions.action: Share concurrent fetches for the same record.
actions.mechanism: Use a bounded per-key in-flight operation instead of duplicate source calls.
actions.implementation: After a cache miss, atomically join or create a fetch keyed by the canonical public record identifier. Share its validated result or failure with waiting requests. Give waiters independent deadlines; cancel the shared fetch only when no waiters remain or its own deadline expires. Remove in-flight metadata on every completion path.
actions.check: Send concurrent requests for one missing key; verify one source call, consistent timeout responses, and no abandoned in-flight entry.
actions.risk: Incorrect key normalization can merge distinct records; slow waiters must not retain record buffers indefinitely.

actions.action: Pause source calls during a sustained outage.
actions.mechanism: Use a circuit breaker with limited recovery probes.
actions.implementation: Configure a failure threshold and cooldown for source timeouts and availability failures. While open, serve only unexpired cache hits and return 503 source_unavailable for misses; continue ordinary expiration and eviction. After cooldown, allow one probe. Close on success or reopen on failure. Do not count legitimate not-found responses as outages.
actions.check: Inject enough failures to open the breaker; verify misses stop calling the source, expired entries disappear, and only one recovery probe runs concurrently.
actions.risk: An overly broad breaker can block healthy source operations; scope it to the actual failure boundary.

actions.action: Reject private or unexpected fields before admitting a record.
actions.mechanism: Make public-data eligibility an explicit schema boundary.
actions.implementation: Restrict fetches to an approved public endpoint and identifier format. Validate source responses against a public-field allowlist before cache insertion; reject unexpected fields rather than caching raw responses. Disable response-body logging, tracing, and disk spill. Use synthetic records for tests and return a non-cacheable upstream-data error on validation failure.
actions.check: Inject an unexpected private field; verify rejection and its absence from cache, logs, traces, and client responses.
actions.risk: Validation cannot guarantee the source never sends private bytes; the endpoint's public-only contract is also necessary.

actions.action: Prevent obsolete fetches from repopulating invalidated records.
actions.mechanism: Fence asynchronous completions with slot generations.
actions.implementation: Assign each reserved cache slot a generation. Increment it whenever the slot is invalidated, cancelled, or reassigned. Accept a source result only if its reservation and generation still match; otherwise discard it without caching. A failed or obsolete completion must not reset any expiration deadline.
actions.check: Delay a fetch, invalidate and reuse its slot, then release the old response; verify it cannot overwrite the replacement or consume an additional slot.
actions.risk: Every insertion and invalidation path must enforce the same generation check.
